planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; this species is more heat-tolerant than many Pieris and performs better than Pieris japonica in warmer gardens.

directions: Native to the mountain forests of Taiwan, this evergreen shrub produces upright, slightly nodding spikes of small white urn-shaped flowers in early spring above glossy, finely toothed dark green leaves, with new growth sometimes flushing bronze-red. It carries a reputation among specialist growers for tolerating summer heat and humidity better than Pieris japonica, making it a worthwhile option in warmer parts of its hardiness range where that species struggles. Grow in consistently moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, sheltered from drying winds and harsh afternoon sun, which can scorch the foliage. Prune only to remove dead wood or to shape lightly right after flowering, since next year's flower buds set soon afterward.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; this low Chinese species spreads slowly into a dense mat and is well suited to a shaded rock garden edge.

directions: A dwarf, mat-forming shrublet from western China, this wintergreen bears small, leathery, wedge-shaped leaves and clusters of tiny white bell flowers in early summer, followed by abundant pure white, snowberry-like fruit that persists well into winter. It stays low and spreads gradually by underground stems, making it a useful small-scale groundcover at the front of a shaded, acidic border or among larger ericaceous shrubs. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial to full shade, since dry soil and strong sun both cause poor growth and leaf bronzing. Top-dress yearly with leaf mold or pine bark fines to maintain the acidity and moisture retention this species needs.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in gritty, humus-rich, well-drained, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; this New Zealand alpine mat-former resents hot, humid summers and needs sharp drainage.

directions: This tiny New Zealand alpine forms a dense, wiry mat of small rounded leaves studded in summer with white or pink-tinged bell flowers, followed by showy berries that range from white through pink to deep red depending on the form. It is best grown in a rock garden, trough, or scree bed where sharp drainage keeps the roots from sitting wet, since this species comes from well-drained subalpine grassland and tussock country and dislikes humid, waterlogged summers. Grow in gritty, acidic, humus-enriched soil in full sun to light shade at higher elevations or afternoon shade in warmer gardens. Top-dress with grit annually and avoid rich, heavy soil, which encourages rot rather than the tight growth this species needs to look its best.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; this Yunnan species, collected by George Forrest, bears aromatic foliage and showy blue-black fruit.

directions: Collected in Yunnan by the plant hunter George Forrest, this upright wintergreen bears glossy, aromatic leaves that release a wintergreen scent when crushed, along with clusters of small white bell flowers in late spring followed by striking blue-black berries that stand out against the dark foliage. It makes a tidy, medium-sized shrub for a shaded woodland border or ericaceous bed, pairing well with rhododendrons and other acid-loving companions. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial to full shade, sheltered from drying wind and the harshest midday sun. Established plants need little routine pruning beyond removing dead or crossing growth.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

planting.note: Plant a male Gaultheria mucronata nearby in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; this female cultivar needs cross-pollination to produce its heavy crop of deep crimson berries.

directions: A female selection of the Chilean shrub long sold as Pernettya mucronata, 'Crimsonia' is grown chiefly for its dense autumn and winter crop of large, deep crimson-red berries set against small, glossy, spine-tipped evergreen leaves. Flowering is modest, with small white bell flowers in late spring giving little hint of the showy fruit display to come, and because this is a female clone, a male Gaultheria mucronata must be planted within a few feet to ensure reliable pollination and fruit set. Grow in moist but well-drained, acidic soil in full sun for the heaviest berry crop, or light shade in hotter climates. Trim lightly in spring only to control size, since berries form on the previous year's growth and hard pruning sacrifices the display.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

planting.note: Plant a male Gaultheria mucronata nearby in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; this female cultivar bears pale pink-blushed white berries and needs a pollinator to fruit well.

directions: This female Chilean shrub cultivar carries an abundant crop of large, rounded berries in a delicate blush of pale pink over white, resembling the sheen of mother-of-pearl, held above small, glossy, dark green evergreen leaves through autumn and winter. Like other Gaultheria mucronata selections it needs a male clone planted nearby for the flowers to set fruit, since the plants are functionally dioecious despite producing some perfect flowers. Grow in moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in full sun for the showiest berry display, tolerating partial shade in hot climates at some cost to flowering and fruit set. Its compact, suckering habit works well massed as a low hedge or informal border planting in an acid-soil garden.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

planting.note: Plant a male Gaultheria mucronata nearby in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; this female cultivar carries bright signal-red berries prized for their vivid winter color.

directions: 'Signal' is a female Chilean shrub selection grown for its bright, pillar-box red berries, among the most vividly colored of the many Gaultheria mucronata cultivars, carried in heavy clusters against small, glossy, dark evergreen leaves from autumn through much of winter. Small white bell flowers appear in late spring but are secondary to the fruit display, and as with all female clones of this species a male plant must be sited nearby to ensure good pollination and a full berry set. Grow in consistently moist, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun for the strongest color, or light shade where summers run hot. The low, spreading, suckering habit suits group plantings, a low informal hedge, or the front of an acid-soil shrub border.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

planting.note: Plant a male Gaultheria mucronata nearby in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; this dwarf, thyme-leaved female cultivar stays low and dense, suiting rock gardens and border edges.

directions: True to its name, 'Thymifolia' carries tiny, densely packed leaves reminiscent of a thyme plant, forming a low, tight mound far smaller than most other Gaultheria mucronata cultivars, and is correspondingly well suited to rock gardens, troughs, or the front edge of an acid-soil border. Small white flowers in late spring give way to a modest but attractive crop of pinkish-white to pale berries in autumn and winter, which, as with other selections of this female-dominant species, forms best when a male plant grows nearby to provide pollen. Grow in moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in full sun to light shade, keeping the compact habit in scale by siting it where it will not be crowded by larger neighbors. Minimal pruning is needed beyond removing the occasional wayward shoot to preserve its neat form.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; this heavy-fruiting selection of American wintergreen was chosen for an especially dense berry set.

directions: This native American wintergreen selection was chosen for producing an especially heavy cascade of bright red berries that persist through winter, set against the same glossy, wintergreen-scented evergreen foliage as the wild species. Small white or pale pink bell flowers hide beneath the leaves in summer before giving way to the fall and winter fruit display that makes this selection stand out in a shaded groundcover planting. Grow in consistently moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade beneath trees or taller shrubs, where it spreads slowly by underground stems to form a low, dense mat. Established plantings need little care beyond an annual topdressing of leaf mold to maintain the acidity and moisture this species depends on.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
